claim: Unc13b WT and KO adrenal chromaffin cells displayed strong chromogranin staining with or without PMA treatment.
source: All four groups (Unc13b WT, Unc13b WT +PMA, Unc13b KO, Unc13b KO +PMA) displayed strong chromogranin staining (Figure 1M–N), with a tendency towards lower staining in the WT +PMA group (p=0.1084), that is the group with the highest secretion (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunostaining experiments, supported by data shown in Figures 1M-N.

claim: There was a tendency towards lower chromogranin staining in the Unc13b WT +PMA group (p=0.1084).
source: All four groups (Unc13b WT, Unc13b WT +PMA, Unc13b KO, Unc13b KO +PMA) displayed strong chromogranin staining (Figure 1M–N), with a tendency towards lower staining in the WT +PMA group (p=0.1084), that is the group with the highest secretion (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunostaining experiments, supported by data shown in Figures 1M-N.

claim: Quantifying the amount of CgA staining close to the membrane did not result in significant differences between Unc13b WT and KO cells with or without PMA.
source: Quantifying the amount of CgA staining close to the membrane also did not result in significant differences (Figure 1O).
evidence: This is a finding from immunostaining experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 1O.

claim: Unc13b KO cells have intact secretory potential with and without PMA.
source: Thus, Unc13b KO cells have intact secretory potential with and without PMA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the chromogranin staining data, representing an inference from the experimental results.

claim: In mouse adrenal chromaffin cells, ubMunc13-2 is required for phorbolester to stimulate secretion.
source: These data show that in mouse adrenal chromaffin cells, ubMunc13-2 is required for phorbolester to stimulate secretion, and in its absence, phorbolester is inhibitory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments on Unc13b WT and KO cells.

claim: In the absence of ubMunc13-2, phorbolester is inhibitory for secretion in chromaffin cells.
source: These data show that in mouse adrenal chromaffin cells, ubMunc13-2 is required for phorbolester to stimulate secretion, and in its absence, phorbolester is inhibitory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments on Unc13b WT and KO cells.

claim: Phorbolesters activate Protein kinase C (PKC), which stimulates secretion.
source: Phorbolesters also activate Protein kinase C (PKC), which stimulates secretion, but apparently this effect does not prevail in the absence of ubMunc13-2, probably due to an overall weak PKC-dependence of secretion from newborn or embryonic mouse chromaffin cells (see Discussion).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PKC activation by phorbolesters.

claim: The PKC stimulation effect does not prevail in the absence of ubMunc13-2, probably due to an overall weak PKC-dependence of secretion from newborn or embryonic mouse chromaffin cells.
source: Phorbolesters also activate Protein kinase C (PKC), which stimulates secretion, but apparently this effect does not prevail in the absence of ubMunc13-2, probably due to an overall weak PKC-dependence of secretion from newborn or embryonic mouse chromaffin cells (see Discussion).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, representing speculation about the mechanism.

claim: PMA stimulation of Unc13a KO cells led to a higher overall secretion level than in Unc13a WT cells treated with PMA.
source: Strikingly, PMA stimulation of Unc13a KO cells led to a higher overall secretion level than in Unc13a WT cells treated with PMA (Figure 2A, traces are mean of all measured cells).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments comparing Unc13a KO and WT cells, supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PMA stimulated the RRP size in both Unc13a WT and Unc13a KO cells.
source: Kinetic analysis showed that PMA stimulated the RRP size in both Unc13a WT and Unc13a KO (Unc13a WT, RRP = 36.9 fF±7.0 fF,+PMA, RRP = 88.5 fF±11.9 fF, Unc13a KO, RRP = 44.4 fF±7.7 fF,+PMA, RRP = 169.2 fF±37.9 fF, Kruskal-Wallis test – Dunn's multiple comparisons test WT vs WT PMA p=0.0091; KO vs KO PMA p=0.0288, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells, supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: On average, the RRP was larger in the Unc13a KO +PMA than in the Unc13a WT +PMA, but the difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: On average, the RRP was larger in the Unc13a KO +PMA than in the Unc13a WT +PMA (169.2 fF ±37.9 fF vs RRP = 88.5 fF±11.9 fF), but the difference did not reach statistical significance.
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells with PMA treatment.

claim: The SRP-size was significantly larger in the Unc13a KO +PMA than in the Unc13a WT +PMA group.
source: The SRP-size was significantly larger in the Unc13a KO +PMA than in the Unc13a WT +PMA group (Unc13a WT, SRP = 29.8 fF±7.9 fF,+PMA, SRP = 45.4 fF±7.0 fF, Unc13a KO, SRP = 40.5 fF±9.5 fF,+PMA, SRP = 95.6 fF±14.2 fF, Kruskal-Wallis test – Dunn's multiple comparisons test: KO vs KO PMA p=0.0048; WT PMA vs KO PMA p=0.0437; WT vs KO PMA p=0.0003, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells, supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The sustained release and the kinetics of RRP and SRP fusion were not significantly different between Unc13a WT and KO conditions with or without PMA.
source: The sustained release and the kinetics of RRP and SRP fusion were not significantly different between conditions (Figure 2C, D and F).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells, supported by data shown in Figures 2C, D and F.

claim: Two-way ANOVA showed that the interaction between genotype and drug application (with or without PMA) was close to significant for RRP size (p=0.0562) and significant for SRP size (p=0.0442) in Unc13a experiments.
source: Indeed, performing this analysis showed that the interaction was close to significant in both cases (p=0.0562 for RRP size and p=0.0442 for SRP size), indicating a likely interaction between the two factors, which was again significant for the SRP.
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis of the Unc13a data.

claim: The secretory amplitude was larger in the Unc13b WT than in Unc13a WT, especially in the presence of PMA.
source: When comparing the two mouse lines, the secretory amplitude was larger in the Unc13b WT than in Unc13a WT, especially in the presence of PMA (Figure 2A vs Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a comparison of data from two different mouse lines, supported by data shown in Figures 1A and 2A.

claim: Unc13a WT and Unc13b WT cultures were not prepared in parallel.
source: However, Unc13a WT and Unc13b WT cultures were not prepared in parallel.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: Unc13a is perinatally lethal.
source: Moreover, because Unc13a is perinatally lethal (Augustin et al., 1999a) we used embryonic animals (18. embryonic day) for Unc13a KO and WT, whereas for Unc13b WT and KO, we used postnatal (P0-P2) animals (Materials and Methods).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Augustin et al., 1999a.

claim: Embryonic animals (18. embryonic day) were used for Unc13a KO and WT experiments.
source: Moreover, because Unc13a is perinatally lethal (Augustin et al., 1999a) we used embryonic animals (18. embryonic day) for Unc13a KO and WT, whereas for Unc13b WT and KO, we used postnatal (P0-P2) animals (Materials and Methods).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: Postnatal (P0-P2) animals were used for Unc13b WT and KO experiments.
source: Moreover, because Unc13a is perinatally lethal (Augustin et al., 1999a) we used embryonic animals (18. embryonic day) for Unc13a KO and WT, whereas for Unc13b WT and KO, we used postnatal (P0-P2) animals (Materials and Methods).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: Unc13a and Unc13b data sets are not directly comparable due to differences in animal age.
source: The data sets are therefore not directly comparable.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental design limitations.

claim: Phorbolester is more potent in the absence of Munc13-1.
source: Overall, phorbolester is more potent in the absence of Munc13-1, consistent with the notion that functional interaction of phorbolester with endogenous Munc13-1 interaction is negative for secretion in chromaffin cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells.

claim: Functional interaction of phorbolester with endogenous Munc13-1 is negative for secretion in chromaffin cells.
source: Overall, phorbolester is more potent in the absence of Munc13-1, consistent with the notion that functional interaction of phorbolester with endogenous Munc13-1 interaction is negative for secretion in chromaffin cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments on Unc13a WT and KO cells.

claim: Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP SFV constructs were previously used for expression in bovine or mouse chromaffin cells.
source: These experiments made use of the Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP Semliki Forest Virus (SFV) constructs previously used for expression in bovine or mouse chromaffin cells (Ashery et al., 2000; Man et al., 2015; Zikich et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Ashery et al., 2000; Man et al., 2015; Zikich et al., 2008.

claim: Before and after the uncaging flash, cells were illuminated by 488 nm light to visualize EGFP.
source: Thus, before and after the uncaging flash, cells were illuminated by 488 nm light to visualize EGFP.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: 488 nm light does not excite fura dyes.
source: This was possible using the same (fura-containing) pipette solution, because 488 nm light does not excite fura dyes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the spectral properties of fura dyes.

claim: The measurements led to a pre-stimulation [Ca2+]i = 0.64 µM±0.09 µM and a post-stimulation [Ca2+]i = 26.8 µM±1.8 µM.
source: Thereby, we established that these measurements led to a pre-stimulation [Ca2+]i = 0.64 µM±0.09 µM and a post-stimulation [Ca2+]i = 26.8 µM±1.8 µM (means ± SEM, n=14) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Successful expression of Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP was verified by Western blotting of SFV-infected HEK-cells.
source: Successful expression of Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP was verified by Western blotting of SFV-infected HEK-cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A), and quantification of EGFP fluorescence from single chromaffin cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental verification, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP, but not Munc13-1-EGFP H567K translocated to the plasma membrane over the course of several minutes upon PMA application.
source: As expected, Munc13-1-EGFP and ubMunc13-2-EGFP, but not Munc13-1-EGFP H567K translocated to the plasma membrane over the course of several minutes.
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The time course of PMA-induced Munc13 translocation most likely reflects the time it takes for PMA to penetrate the cell, combined with the time it takes for Munc13 to diffuse to the plasma membrane in the absence of increased [Ca2+].
source: This time course most likely reflects the time it takes for PMA to penetrate the cell, combined with the time it takes for Munc13 to diffuse to the plasma membrane in the absence of increased [Ca2+].
evidence: This is an interpretation of the imaging data, representing speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The main effect of PMA is on secretion amplitude, not kinetics.
source: Since the capacitance measurements above indicated that the main effect of PMA is on secretion amplitude, not kinetics (see also Nagy et al., 2006), we simplified the analysis and only distinguished between burst secretion (first 1 s secretion after Ca2+ uncaging, corresponding approximately to RRP and SRP fusion) and sustained secretion (last 4 s of secretion), as well as total secretion (the sum of burst and sustained release).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citation to Nagy et al., 2006.

claim: Expression of ubMunc13-2-EGFP in Unc13b KO cells resulted in large secretory amplitude, ~800 fF.
source: Expression of ubMunc13-2-EGFP in Unc13b KO cells resulted in large secretory amplitude, ~800 fF (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13b KO cells expressing ubMunc13-2-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In response to PMA, secretion in ubMunc13-2-EGFP expressing Unc13b KO cells was increased even further, resulting in an increase in burst size and total secretion.
source: In response to PMA, secretion was increased even further, resulting in an increase in burst size, total and sustained secretion; the two former effects were statistically significant (Burst - Overexpressed (OE) ubMunc13-2-EGFP: 239.09 fF ±25.96 fF,+PMA: 628.72 fF ±119.64 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0314; Total - OE ubMunc13-2 EGFP: 808.93 fF ±107.82 fF,+PMA: 1344.53 fF ±178.70 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0479; Sustained - OE ubMunc13-2-EGFP: 570.22 fF ±87.67 fF; 714.66±89.75, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.2992; Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13b KO cells expressing ubMunc13-2-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ubMunc13-2-EGFP was present in the cytosol before Ca2+ uncaging.
source: ubMunc13-2-EGFP was present in the cytosol (Figure 3A top panels), but upon uncaging, part of the protein trafficked to the plasma membrane within a few seconds, with a kinetics roughly matching sustained release - in Figure 3B the normalized PM fluorescence was replotted behind the capacitance trace to allow a comparison (Figure 3A–B; Figure 3—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Upon Ca2+ uncaging, part of ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficked to the plasma membrane within a few seconds, with a kinetics roughly matching sustained release.
source: ubMunc13-2-EGFP was present in the cytosol (Figure 3A top panels), but upon uncaging, part of the protein trafficked to the plasma membrane within a few seconds, with a kinetics roughly matching sustained release - in Figure 3B the normalized PM fluorescence was replotted behind the capacitance trace to allow a comparison (Figure 3A–B; Figure 3—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figures 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Upon application of PMA, ubMunc13-2-EGFP was already at the plasma membrane and did not traffic further upon Ca2+ increase.
source: Upon application of PMA, ubMunc13-2-EGFP was already at the plasma membrane and did not traffic further upon Ca2+ increase (Figure 3A bottom panels, Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figures 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Ca2+-dependent trafficking of ubMunc13-2-EGFP was highly significant when comparing the no PMA group to the PMA group.
source: This showed that Ca2+-dependent trafficking was highly significant (Mann-Whitney test: p<0.0001; Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of Munc13-1-EGFP in Unc13a KO cells resulted in approximately 400 fF secretion.
source: Expression of Munc13-1-EGFP in Unc13a KO cells resulted in approximately 400 fF secretion (Figure 4B), more than in the Unc13a WT (Figure 2), although we here compare experiments not carried out in parallel.
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a KO cells expressing Munc13-1-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Munc13-1-EGFP localized to the cytosol, with part of the protein found in larger accumulations in some, but not all cells.
source: Munc13-1-EGFP localized to the cytosol, with part of the protein found in larger accumulations in some, but not all cells (compare different examples in Figure 4A, Figure 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The accumulations of Munc13-1-EGFP might be related to the higher average expression level of Munc13-1 compared to ubMunc13-2.
source: We speculated that the accumulations might be related to the higher average expression level of Munc13-1 compared to ubMunc13-2, as assessed by cellular EGFP fluorescence (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is speculation about the cause of the accumulations, based on data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Upon PMA application, part of Munc13-1-EGFP localized to the plasma membrane.
source: Upon PMA application, part of the protein localized to the plasma membrane (Figure 4A; Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Expression of Munc13-1-EGFP in cells from CD1-mice caused a clear and statistically significant increase in total and sustained secretion.
source: As a further indication that Munc13-1-EGFP is functional, we expressed it in cells from CD1-mice (an outbred mouse strain). Expression caused a clear and statistically significant increase in total and sustained secretion (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on CD1 cells expressing Munc13-1-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overall little membrane trafficking was induced by increasing calcium in Munc13-1-EGFP expressing cells.
source: Although some individual cells displayed EGFP-Munc13-1 trafficking (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), overall little membrane trafficking was induced by increasing calcium in Munc13-1-EGFP expressing cells (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments, supported by data shown in Figures 4B-C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Following PMA-application, total, burst and sustained secretion were reduced in Munc13-1-EGFP expressing Unc13a KO cells; the effects on total and burst secretion were statistically significant.
source: Following PMA-application, total, burst and sustained secretion were reduced; the effects on total and burst secretion were statistically significant (Burst - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 136.92 fF ±26.09 fF,+PMA: 68.34 fF ±9.10 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0117; Total - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 414.22 fF ±69.47 fF,+PMA: 219.53 fF ±34.35 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0182; Sustained - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 273.30 fF ±52.75 fF; 150.9±32.07, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0793; Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13a KO cells expressing Munc13-1-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figures 4B and D.

claim: PMA-induced stimulation of Munc13-1 is inhibitory for DV secretion in chromaffin cells.
source: These data indicate that PMA-induced stimulation of Munc13-1 is inhibitory for DV secretion in chromaffin cells, in agreement with findings above in the Unc13a and Unc13b mouse lines.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments on Munc13-1-EGFP expressing cells.

claim: Expression of the Munc13-1 H567K mutation in adrenal chromaffin cells from CD1 mice showed no effect of PMA.
source: As a control, we expressed the Munc13-1 H567K mutation, which does not bind to phorbolesters (Betz et al., 1998) in adrenal chromaffin cells from CD1 mice. Upon expression, there was no effect of PMA (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), which agrees with previous data from bovine chromaffin cells (Bauer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on CD1 cells expressing Munc13-1 H567K-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and citations.

claim: The Munc13-1 H567K mutation does not bind to phorbolesters.
source: As a control, we expressed the Munc13-1 H567K mutation, which does not bind to phorbolesters (Betz et al., 1998) in adrenal chromaffin cells from CD1 mice.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Betz et al., 1998.

claim: Evidence from both Munc13-1-EGFP overexpression and Unc13a KO as well as Unc13b KO indicate that PMA interacting with Munc13-1 is inhibitory.
source: Thus, evidence from both Munc13-1-EGFP overexpression and Unc13a KO as well as Unc13b KO indicate that PMA interacting with Munc13-1 is inhibitory, whereas PMA interacting with ubMunc13-2 is positive for DV secretion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: PMA interacting with ubMunc13-2 is positive for DV secretion.
source: Thus, evidence from both Munc13-1-EGFP overexpression and Unc13a KO as well as Unc13b KO indicate that PMA interacting with Munc13-1 is inhibitory, whereas PMA interacting with ubMunc13-2 is positive for DV secretion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: ubMunc13-2 supports more secretion than Munc13-1 upon overexpression in parallel experiments.
source: Since ubMunc13-2 supports more secretion than Munc13-1 upon overexpression in parallel experiments (Man et al., 2015), it is possible that the apparent negative effect of Munc13-1 could be due to competition with ubMunc13-2, because targeting Munc13-1 to the plasma membrane with PMA might displace the more potent ubMunc13-2.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Man et al., 2015.

claim: The apparent negative effect of Munc13-1 could be due to competition with ubMunc13-2, because targeting Munc13-1 to the plasma membrane with PMA might displace the more potent ubMunc13-2.
source: Since ubMunc13-2 supports more secretion than Munc13-1 upon overexpression in parallel experiments (Man et al., 2015), it is possible that the apparent negative effect of Munc13-1 could be due to competition with ubMunc13-2, because targeting Munc13-1 to the plasma membrane with PMA might displace the more potent ubMunc13-2.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of Munc13-1's negative effect.

claim: When Munc13-1-EGFP was expressed in Unc13b KO cells, PMA application led to a significant decrease in total and sustained secretion, but the secretory burst was unaffected.
source: Even under these circumstances, PMA application led to a significant decrease in total and sustained secretion, but the secretory burst was now unaffected (Burst - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 104.64 fF ±20.58 fF,+PMA: 104.47 fF ±18.30 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.8280; Total - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 452.45 fF ±62.21 fF,+PMA: 210.43 fF ±50.40 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p<0.0001; Sustained - OE Munc13-1-EGFP: 347.8 fF ±63.42 fF;+PMA: 106±38.75, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0001; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Unc13b KO cells expressing Munc13-1-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The ability of PMA and Munc13-1 to suppress the burst might be due to displacement of ubMunc13-2.
source: Thus, the ability of PMA and Munc13-1 to suppress the burst might be due to displacement of ubMunc13-2, but ubMunc13-2 is not required for the overall inhibitory nature of PMAs interaction with Munc13-1.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data comparing Munc13-1-EGFP expression in Unc13a KO and Unc13b KO cells.

claim: ubMunc13-2 is not required for the overall inhibitory nature of PMAs interaction with Munc13-1.
source: Thus, the ability of PMA and Munc13-1 to suppress the burst might be due to displacement of ubMunc13-2, but ubMunc13-2 is not required for the overall inhibitory nature of PMAs interaction with Munc13-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments on Unc13b KO cells expressing Munc13-1-EGFP.

claim: Syt7 is involved in calcium and phorbolester-induced priming of chromaffin cells DVs.
source: We previously showed that Syt7 is involved in calcium and phorbolester-induced priming of chromaffin cells DVs (Tawfik et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, supported by citation to Tawfik et al., 2021.

claim: Expression of ubMunc13-2 resulted in massive secretion in both the Syt7 KO and WT.
source: As previously reported (Tawfik et al., 2021), expression of ubMunc13-2 resulted in massive secretion in both the Syt7 KO and WT, but secretion was delayed in Syt7 KO (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Syt7 KO and WT cells, supported by data shown in Figure 6B and citation to Tawfik et al., 2021.

claim: Secretion was delayed in Syt7 KO cells expressing ubMunc13-2 compared to Syt7 WT.
source: As previously reported (Tawfik et al., 2021), expression of ubMunc13-2 resulted in massive secretion in both the Syt7 KO and WT, but secretion was delayed in Syt7 KO (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Syt7 KO and WT cells, supported by data shown in Figure 6B and citation to Tawfik et al., 2021.

claim: The burst size, as defined by secretion within the first second, was significantly reduced in Syt7 KO cells expressing EGFP-ubMunc13-2 compared to Syt7 WT expressing EGFP-ubMunc13-2.
source: As a result, the burst size, as defined by secretion within the first second, was significantly reduced in Syt7 KO cells expressing EGFP-ubMunc13-2 compared to Syt7 WT expressing EGFP-ubMunc13-2 (Burst - OE ubMunc13-2-eGFP in Syt7 WT: 317.01 fF ±53.24 fF, OE Munc13-2-EGFP in Syt7 KO: 150.21 fF ±24.91 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0286, Figure 6D; for other values see Source Data File).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Syt7 KO and WT cells expressing ubMunc13-2-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In spite of the delayed secretion in the Syt7 KO, ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking was unchanged.
source: Imaging showed that in spite of the delayed secretion in the Syt7 KO, ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking was unchanged (Figure 6A–B), and – consequently – ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking preceded exocytosis in the Syt7 KO ubMunc13-2 overexpressing cells (Figure 6B bottom panel).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments on Syt7 KO cells, supported by data shown in Figures 6A-B.

claim: ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking preceded exocytosis in the Syt7 KO ubMunc13-2 overexpressing cells.
source: Imaging showed that in spite of the delayed secretion in the Syt7 KO, ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking was unchanged (Figure 6A–B), and – consequently – ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking preceded exocytosis in the Syt7 KO ubMunc13-2 overexpressing cells (Figure 6B bottom panel).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging experiments on Syt7 KO cells, supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Calcium-dependent ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking is independent of Syt7.
source: Therefore, calcium-dependent ubMunc13-2-EGFP trafficking is independent of Syt7.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the imaging experiments on Syt7 KO cells.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitations failed to identify any interaction between b/ubMunc13-2 and Syt7, or between Munc13-1 and Syt7.
source: To investigate this further, we performed co-immunoprecipations between b/ubMunc13-2 and Syt7, as well as between Munc13-1 and Syt7 (Materials and methods). However, we failed to identify any interaction (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from co-immunoprecipitation experiments, supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Any functional interaction between Syt7 and Munc13-2 does not seem to involve direct stable binding or co-trafficking, but transient interactions cannot be ruled out.
source: Therefore, any functional interaction between Syt7 and Munc13-2 does not seem to involve direct stable binding or co-trafficking, but transient interactions cannot be ruled out.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-immunoprecipitation results.

claim: In Syt7 KO cells expressing ubMunc13-2-EGFP, PMA was strongly inhibitory for secretion.
source: Strikingly, in these cells, PMA was strongly inhibitory for secretion (Figure 7D), leading to a statistically significant decrease in total and sustained secretion, whereas the burst was non-significantly reduced (Burst - OE ubMunc13-2-EGFP in Syt7 KO: 220.51 fF ±51.60 fF,+PMA: 185.45 fF ±53.19 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.3989; Total - OE ubMunc13-2-EGFP in Syt7 KO: 896.60 fF ±199.86 fF,+PMA: 223.03 fF ±53.60 fF, Mann-Whitney test: p=0.0002; Sustained - OE ubMunc13-2-EGFP in Syt7 KO: 676.34 fF ±156.89 fF;+PMA: 37.43±15.53, Mann-Whitney test: p<0.0001; Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments on Syt7 KO cells expressing ubMunc13-2-EGFP, supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: ubMunc13-2 trafficked to the PM after a calcium increase in Syt7 KO cells.
source: Similar to data obtained above, ubMunc13-2 trafficked to the PM after a calcium increase (Figure 7A–C).
